channel.title: Pier & Point · Weill Neurosciences Building
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Weill Neurosciences Building (Mission Bay), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Weill Neurosciences Building: The record said the building opened in October 2021
item.description: The record said the building opened in October 2021; UCSF Health's own Weill page says it opened its doors in July 2021 (the October date matches a UCSF news release that could not be read). The size range is now 282,000-283,000 sq ft (Architectural Record 283,000, DPR 282,000). The March 2016 Regents item is described as an agenda item requesting approval, since it does not record the vote. The aerial site photo's credit now names USDA's Farm Production and Conservation Business Center, the publisher on data.gov's NAIP record, and the other aerial's caption no longer says 'from a departing flight'. The map notes now cite UCSF Health and CEQAnet for the building name, block 23A and the neurosurgery clinic. Source: UCSF Health, Weill Neurosciences Building (https://www.ucsfhealth.org/lp/weill-neurosciences-building); UCSF Health, Neurosurgery Mission Bay - Fourth St. (https://www.ucsfhealth.org/locations/neurosurgery-mission-bay-fourth-st); Architectural Record, 2021-10-27 (https://www.architecturalrecord.com/articles/15366-ucsf-joan-sanford-i-weill-neurosciences-building-by-smithgroup-with-mark-cavagnero-associates); DPR Construction, UCSF Block 23A Neurosciences Research Building (https://www.dpr.com/projects/ucsf-block-23a-neurosciences-research-building); UC Regents item, 2016-03-24 (https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/regmeet/mar16/gb1.pdf); USDA NAIP Imagery catalog record (https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/national-agriculture-imagery-program-naip-imagery); CEQAnet SCH 2013092047 (https://ceqanet.lci.ca.gov/2013092047/15).

item.title: Added · Weill Neurosciences Building: In May 2017 the UC Regents approved a total project budget…
item.description: In May 2017 the UC Regents approved a total project budget of $357.6M for the Weill Neurosciences Building, funded from $141.6M in external financing, $175M in gifts and $41M in campus funding. Source: UC San Francisco, UC Regents Approve Building Plans for 3 Projects in Mission Bay, Dogpatch, 2017-05 (https://www.ucsf.edu/news/2017/05/407096/uc-regents-approve-building-plans-3-projects-mission-bay-dogpatch).
item.source: UC San Francisco, UC Regents Approve Building Plans for 3 Projects in Mission Bay, Dogpatch, 2017-05 (https://www.ucsf.edu/news/2017/05/407096/uc-regents-approve-building-plans-3-projects-mission-bay-dogpatch)

item.title: Complete · Weill Neurosciences Building: Joan and Sanford I. Weill Neurosciences… (Jul 2021)
item.description: Joan and Sanford I. Weill Neurosciences Building opens its doors (UCSF Health: 'It opened its doors in July 2021'); it houses medical clinics, research centers and laboratories (Jul 2021). Source: UCSF Health; UC San Francisco, 2021-10.

item.title: Milestone · Weill Neurosciences Building: Construction completed, per architecture… (~Jun 2021)
item.description: Construction completed, per architecture trade press (Architectural Record) (~Jun 2021). Source: Architectural Record, 2021-10-27.

item.title: Planned · Weill Neurosciences Building: UC Regents Committee on Grounds and… (Mar 24, 2016)
item.description: UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings is asked to approve $21,000,000 in preliminary-plans funding for the Mission Bay Neurosciences Research Building (Block 23A) – a 270,000 gsf, six-story building on the Block 23A surface parking lot that became this building (agenda item for the March 24, 2016 meeting; it does not record the vote) – with full budget, financing and design/CEQA approval expected in March 2017 and construction targeted for fall 2017; the full budget and design item went to the Regents for their May 17, 2017 meeting instead (Mar 24, 2016). Source: The Regents of the University of California, 2016-03-24; The Regents of the University of California, 2017-05-17.
